newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs firm, Med Suezmaxes busy.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs firm, Med Suezmaxes busy.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were firm on Wednesday with strong interest to Singapore and South Korea, brokers said.
Two modern VLCCs, the Maersk Navarin and the Flores, were fixed at W60 to Singapore for SPC and BP respectively, some 10 points above the rate for older vessels, they added.
One broker said this was a further sign of a growing preference for quality tonnage in Asia, as has been apparent to Japan and South Korea for some time.
Mideast/Japan VLCCs were steady at W62.5/65. The Karoline was fixed for 330,000 tonnes to UKC at W48.75 for Shell.
The 275,000 tonne Argo Pallas was done for Fina on a COA basis.
The Mediterranean was also active with 130,000 tonners fixed at W90/92.5, up almost 10 points, for a Sidi Kreir/Italy trip and above W100 for a shorter cross-Med hop.
"There is less and less tonnage around. We are certainly on an upward trend," another broker said.

The North Sea/U.S. sector was quiet, with 80,000 tonners steady at W136. There was little VLCC activity on this route but in the Suezmax sector 134,000 tonnes was fixed on the Romea Champion at W94.5 for Sun.
Fuel oil was also quiet and steady, with 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont at W205 and cross-Med at W200. "There has been no fresh enquiry but at least rates have not fallen," one broker said.
In the Caribbean, 70,000 tonnes upcoast was little changed at W142.5, with 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes up slightly at W190 from W185.
